components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, glowing control — primary action per view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: #e53333; color: #1a0505; font-family: Syne, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 0 18px color-mix(in srgb, #e53333 34%, transparent); transition: background .15s cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1), box-shadow .15s cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1), transform .1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { box-shadow: 0 0 28px color-mix(in srgb, #e53333 52%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #e53333; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, #e53333 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: .5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The workhorse control — most buttons are not primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.045); border-radius: 10px; background: transparent; color: #8896aa; font-family: Syne, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background .15s, border-color .15s, color .15s, transform .1s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #171b28; border-color: color-mix(in srgb, #e53333 40%, transparent); color: #dce4f0; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, #e53333 70%, transparent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-outline:active { color: #e53333; transform: translateY(0); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Lowest-emphasis control; icon buttons and inline toolbar actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: transparent; color: #8896aa; cursor: pointer; transition: background .15s, color .15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #171b28; color: #dce4f0; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, #e53333 70%, transparent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-ghost:active { color: #e53333; }

components.name: Search Input

narrative.overview: Mission Control is two surfaces sharing one shell: a tight instrument cluster (tasks, homelab services, agent logs, system gauges) where density is the point, and a full-bleed media theatre (hero backdrops, 68–84px titles, auto-hiding chrome, HLS into the hero background). The single red accent is the wire between them — it marks the live thing on the console and the play button in the theatre, and almost nothing else. The room is dark by default: near-black surfaces separated by tonal steps and hairline borders, never drop shadows. This is a flat system; the older 'neumorphism' language in CLAUDE.md has been fully replaced. It rejects soft embossing, pastel SaaS gradients, glassmorphism-as-default, and decorative motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, near-black tonal layering; hairline borders instead of shadows.
A single family (Syne) carries display, UI, labels, and tabular figures.
One red accent, used as a live-status signal — never decoration.
Extreme density on the console side; full-bleed cinema on the media side.
Fixed rem type scale for UI; fluid only where the media hero is genuinely cinematic.

rules.name: The One Wire Rule
rules.body: Signal Red is a signal, not a color you decorate with. It marks the single live or primary thing in a view; its glow is reserved for exactly those. If two red things compete for 'the live one,' one is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Green Rule
rules.body: Success is red (--ok: var(--accent)); there is no green token. Status is carried by red (live/ok), amber (warn), pink-red (bad), and blue (info).

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number in a column or that updates in place uses the mono role with tnum on; figures must not reflow as their value changes.

rules.name: The Tracked-Label Rule
rules.body: Structural labels are uppercase, tracking 0.16em, and --muted. Small, spaced, dim is how a label signals 'I am chrome, not content.'

rules.name: The Flat-Console Rule
rules.body: On the console, depth is tonal + hairline only. If you reach for a black box-shadow to separate two panels, fix the surface color, not the shadow.

rules.name: The Glow-Means-Live Rule
rules.body: A red glow is never ambient decoration; it appears only on live or primary elements. A resting, non-primary surface never glows.

dos: Do keep the app dark-first — Console Black (#09090d) is the page; surfaces climb the tonal ladder from there.
Do convey panel depth with a tonal step + a single hairline border, never a drop shadow.
Do reserve Signal Red (#e53333) and its glow for the one live or primary element in a view.
Do set numeric/columnar values in the mono role with tabular figures (tnum).
Do set structural labels UPPERCASE, tracking-5 (0.16em), --muted.
Do give every interactive component its full state set (default / hover / focus-visible red ring / active / disabled / loading).
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion — the media hover and skeleton shimmer already collapse to near-instant.
donts: Don't reintroduce neumorphism — no soft dual embossed shadows on surfaces.
Don't use a black box-shadow to separate console panels; the media-card hover lift is the only sanctioned black drop shadow.
Don't add a green — success is red; status lives in the four-signal vocabulary.
Don't decorate with the red accent or its glow — a resting, non-primary surface never glows.
Don't set body copy in --muted; use --ink / --ink-soft.
Don't flip the light theme to white paper — it is a cool slate that keeps the console mood in daylight.
Don't introduce a second type family or a real monospace face — one Syne, many weights, tnum for figures.
Don't use glassmorphism as a default surface; backdrop-blur is reserved for the modal/drawer overlay scrim.
